problems.jsonl.statement: Improve the bound Var(log Z_n) = O(n/log n) for directed polymers in random environment in general dimension to a power improvement n^{1-eps}.
problems.jsonl.status_search: In d = 1+1 with exactly solvable weights (log-gamma, exponential last-passage) the exponent 2/3 (variance n^{2/3}) is a theorem; for general weights in any dimension the BKS-type n/log n remains the best general bound to this session's knowledge; cf. the FPP variance problem in the Codex campaign (P-a/ chi = 1/3 target).
problems.jsonl.title: Fluctuation exponent of directed polymers beyond the logarithmic improvement

attempts.jsonl.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
attempts.jsonl.method: Same block as the first-passage percolation sublinear variance problem; record the exact reduction.
attempts.jsonl.obstruction: Quantitative chaos rate or transversal fluctuation bound unavailable outside integrable models.
attempts.jsonl.result: The n/log n bound is the BKS entropy method; a power improvement n^{1-eps} would follow from a chaos exponent: if the polymer measure decorrelates under a noise of size n^{-eps'} on the environment (superconcentration with a rate), Talagrand's/Chatterjee's equivalence gives Var(log Z_n) <= n^{1-eps}. Conversely, the variance exponent is tied to the transversal fluctuation exponent by the KPZ scaling relation chi = 2 xi - 1 (Chatterjee 2013 proved the relation rigorously for FPP under existence of the exponents), so a power improvement needs a quantitative transversal-fluctuation bound xi < 1 with an explicit gap, which is known only in the exactly solvable models. The obstruction is the same wall the campaign records for FPP; no new input.

sources.jsonl.title: Chatterjee: Chaos, concentration and multiple valleys, 2008, with open questions
